sentences.text: Fissuravis is an extinct bird genus belonging to the family Lithornithidae, a group closely related to modern ratites.
The species defining this genus is Fissuravis weigelti.
Unlike its relatives, Fissuravis was a capable flyer.
Remnants of the coracoid — a bone in the shoulder girdle — suggest it had powerful flight muscles and likely engaged in soaring flight.
The genus was named by Mayr in 2007.
Fossils come from the Walbeck Paleocene deposits in Germany.
Fissuravis lived between 61.66 and 59.24 million years ago during the Selandian stage of the Paleocene epoch.
